title: Business AI adoption is concentrated by firm size and sector rather than spreading evenly
source_unit: Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey employer businesses, December 2025-May 3, 2026
geography: United States, with sector, state, and firm-size estimates

observations.period: December 2025-May 3, 2026 BTOS data; Census story published May 26, 2026

denominator.unit: nationally representative employer businesses excluding farms; published summary does not provide the analytic respondent count

overall_current_ai_use.unit: percent of employer businesses reporting AI use in the prior two weeks

expected_ai_use.unit: percent of businesses expecting to use AI in the next six months

large_firm_use.value: 37% of firms with at least 250 employees; 32% of firms with 100-249 employees as of May 3

sector_use.value: Information 39.7%; Finance and Insurance 33.9%; national rate 19.8% as of May 3

small_firm_boundary.value: less than 20% of firms with four or fewer employees reported use

observations.method: Census BTOS biweekly representative survey of employer businesses; current use and expected use are reported by firm size and sector. Census revised AI question wording in November 2025 from production use to any business function.
observations.uncertainty: The wording change limits direct comparisons across the break. Adoption does not show effective use, task quality, worker displacement, productivity, profitability, or power redistribution.
observations.subgroup: Employer businesses by size and sector; farms excluded.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher reported use in large and information-intensive firms may reflect resources, task mix, reporting capacity, or survey interpretation rather than a universal technology advantage.

related_sources.claim: Census provides BTOS national, sector, state, metro, and AI-supplement downloads.

boundary: This record adds a firm-capacity and labor-exposure layer: AI adoption is stratified by size and sector. It does not show realized productivity, worker outcomes, consumer prices, local infrastructure, or political meaning.
